1) Aggrieved by the impugned Award, dated 21.04.2011, passed in M.V.O.P. No. 11 of 2006 on the
file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-VIII Additional District Judge, Chittoor, whereby,
the
claim of the Claimants was dismissed by the Tribunal; this instant Appeal is preferred by the claim petitioners, questioning the legal validity of the Award passed by the Tribunal.
2) For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the Appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3) The claim petitioners filed the petition under Section 166(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [the 'M.V. Act'], read with Rule 475 of the A.P.M.V. Rules, 1989 [the 'Rules'] against the sole respondent claiming compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- for the death of one K. Sarojamma, [the 'deceased'], who is the mother of the Claimants in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 30.03.2005.

4) Facts germane to dispose of the Appeal may briefly be stated as follows: -
i. On 30.03.2005 at about 00.50 hours, while the deceased was going by walk near MSR Junction, Chittoor, from her house, to go to her daughter's house, the driver of the A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No.AP11 Z 4501, belonging to Alipiri Depot,
coming from Bangalore side to Chittoor, drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the back side of the deceased, causing bleeding injuries all over the body of the deceased, who subsequently succumbed at Government Head Quarters Hospital, Chittoor.
ii. The Chittoor Traffic Police, registered a case in crime No.41 of 2005 against the driver of A.P.S.R.T.C. bus for the offence punishable under Section 304-A of Indian Penal Code, 1860 ['I.P.C.'].

The respondent is the owner of the offending bus; hence,
the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
5) The respondent filed the written statement with a plea that it is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners and prays to dismiss the petition.

6) Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the Tribunal:

sentences.text: Whether the accident in question was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus bearing No. AP11 Z 4501?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation? If so, to what quantum?

And from whom?
7) During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioners,
PW1 and PW2 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A5 were marked.
On behalf of the respondent, no witness was examined, but, however, Ex.B1 was marked.

8) At the culmination of the enquiry, based on the material available on record, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the claimants failed to prove negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and, accordingly, dismissed the petition of the claim petitioners.
Aggrieved against the dismissal of claim petition, the appellants/petitioners preferred the present appeal.

9) Heard learned counsels for both the parties and perused the record.
10) Now, the point for determination is:
i) Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?
ii) Whether the appellants/claimants are entitled to any amount of compensation, as prayed for?
11) POINT Nos. (i) & (ii): The case of the claimants is that, the deceased K.
Sarojamma is their mother.

At about 12.50 A.M., while she was going on the left side of the road near MSR Junction by walk, from her house, to go to her daughter's house, at that time one A.P.S.R.T.C. bus bearing registration No. AP11 Z 4501 of Alipiri Depot coming from Bangalore side towards Chittoor, driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against the back side of the deceased, as a result,
the deceased sustained bleeding injuries all over her body and at Government Hospital, Chittoor, she died.
12) In order to prove the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending driver, the petitioners relied on the evidence of PW1 and PW2.

Ex.A1 - certified copy of F.I.R. goes to show that,
a crime was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C. bus.

The material on record reveals that the Sub-Inspector of Police filed charge- sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle A.P.S.R.T.C. bus in a criminal court vide C.C. No. 160 of 2005 on the file of the V Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Chittoor.

entities.text: V Additional Judicial First Class Magistrate, Chittoor
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ex. B1
filed by the respondent/A.P.S.R.T.C.
supports the same.

2 13)

entities.text: S.Ramesh Babu vs The Ap State Transport Corporation on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the evidence of PW2, who is an eye witness to the incident, his evidence is that, the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of A.P.S.R.T.C. bus and the driver of the bus drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the deceased.

The Tribunal held in its order that, in Ex.B1 - certified copy of the calendar and judgment in C.C. No. 160 of 2005, the PW2 in the present case was examined as 'PW3' in that case and he turned hostile in the said criminal case.
Therefore, it is not safe to rely on the evidence of PW2 in a claim petition filed by the claimants.
14) The law is well settled that, mere acquittal in a criminal case does not lead to an automatic inference that there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
The standard of proof required is entirely different from the Criminal Court.
15) The law is well settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sunita & Ors. Vs. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Ors.1 and Kusumlata & Ors Vs. Satbir & Ors2.

entities.text: Sunita & Ors. Vs. Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation & Ors.1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In those decisions, it was held that, strict rules of evidence as applicable in a criminal trial, are not applicable in motor accident compensation cases, i.e., to say, "the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases".
(2020)13 SCC 486 (2011) 3 SCC 646 16)

Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal, in its order, that since PW2 herein, who was examined as PW3 in a criminal case turned hostile, it is not safe to rely on the evidence of PW2 herein, is unreasonable.

Therefore, on considering the entire material on record, I am of the considered view that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of A.P.S.R.T.C.,
bus, in which the deceased died in a road accident.

17) The learned Standing Counsel for the A.P.S.R.T.C. would submit that, the Claimants are none other than the major sons of the deceased, aged about 30 and 35 years respectively, and the deceased was aged about 60 years by the date of claim petition.
18) No doubt, the material on record reveals the age of the deceased is '60' years by the date of accident and the claimants are aged about 30 and 35 years respectively, and they are majors, and the deceased was none other than the mother of the claimants.
As per Section 166 of M.V. Act, the legal representative can file a petition for compensation in the event of death resulting from an accident.
However, the Tribunal may limit the compensation if it is determined that the claimants are not dependents on the deceased.
Herein, the deceased was aged about 60 years by the date of accident and the claimants are major sons aged about 30 and 35 years, respectively.

Since, the incident in question is proved due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of A.P.S.R.T.C., bus; the claimants are entitled to an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards 'loss of estate, love and affection' and Rs.20,000/-
towards 'funeral expenses'.

The said amount has to be paid by the sole respondent/A.P.S.R.T.C.
19)
In the result, the appeal is partly allowed setting aside the Award of the Tribunal, dated 21.04.2011, passed in M.V.O.P. No. 11 of 2006.

Consequently, the claim application in M.V.O.P. No.
S.Ramesh Babu vs The Ap State Transport Corporation on 17 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53747009/
3 11 of 2006 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-VIII Additional District Judge,
Chittoor, is partly allowed by granting compensation of Rs.70,000/- to the claimants towards total compensation with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
